title: From Vivek Oberoi to Shobana: The Character Actors Powering India's Biggest Hits
excerpt: A new generation of scene-stealing performances by veteran actors is reshaping how audiences discover talent across Bollywood, South cinema, and streaming platforms.
body:
• Vivek Oberoi, Shobana, and Panchayat's Faisal Malik represent a generation of actors whose brief but memorable appearances are powering some of India's biggest current productions.
  • Faisal Malik, beloved as Prahlad Chacha in Panchayat, has been cast as Kumbhakarna in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana alongside Ranbir Kapoor.
  • Vivek Oberoi is set for a major 2026 with roles in Ramayana (as Vibhishan), Spirit with Prabhas, and Mastii 4.
  • The trend reflects Indian cinema's shift toward ensemble-driven storytelling where supporting performances define the audience experience.

The Art of the Scene-Stealer

In an era when Indian cinema is increasingly driven by franchise thinking and star power, a quieter revolution is taking place in the margins. Character actors — performers whose brief appearances, sharp cameos, and supporting turns often define the most memorable moments in a production — are enjoying an unprecedented moment of recognition.

https://x.com/vivekoberoi/status/2082736850838736929

A recent feature spotlighting actors from Vivek Oberoi to the legendary Shobana and Panchayat star Faisal Malik highlights how these performers are connecting the dots between Bollywood's mainstream blockbusters, South Indian cinema's expanding national footprint, and the streaming platforms that have given character actors their largest audiences yet.

Faisal Malik's Remarkable Rise

Few trajectories illustrate this shift better than Faisal Malik's. Known to millions as Prahlad Chacha — the lovable, scheming village politician in Amazon Prime Video's Panchayat — Malik has parlayed that breakout role into a part in one of Indian cinema's most ambitious productions: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, where he will play Kumbhakarna opposite Ranbir Kapoor's Ram.

Panchayat, which crossed 12 million views in its third season's first week and is now filming its fourth, owes much of its appeal to the ensemble performances that make the fictional village of Phulera feel lived-in. Malik's Prahlad is arguably the show's most beloved character, a testament to what a skilled actor can build from a supporting role.

Vivek Oberoi's Second Act

Vivek Oberoi, who first commanded attention with his debut in Ram Gopal Varma's Company in 2002, has reinvented himself as a character actor of considerable range. His 2026 slate includes Vibhishan in Ramayana, a role in Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Spirit alongside Prabhas, and a reunion with Riteish Deshmukh and Aftab Shivdasani in Mastii 4.

Oberoi donated his entire fee from Ramayana to children's cancer treatment, describing the project as a labor of devotion. The gesture reflects a broader pattern among mid-career actors finding renewed purpose through mythological and historical productions.

"I now choose work out of passion and peace, not pressure or compulsion."

— Vivek Oberoi

South Cinema's Gift to the Ensemble

Shobana, the National Award-winning actress and Bharatanatyam dancer, exemplifies how South Indian cinema has long valued the character performance. Her ability to command a scene in limited screen time has made her a reference point for a generation of performers working across languages.

The streaming era has been particularly kind to this class of actor. Platforms like Prime Video, Netflix, and JioHotstar have built shows around ensemble casts where every member contributes to the texture of the world — a model that rewards precisely the kind of work character actors excel at.
nri_angle: For diaspora audiences who primarily consume Indian content through streaming platforms, these character actors have become familiar faces transcending language barriers, with shows like Panchayat developing devoted NRI followings.
